samples.summary: Relaxing `seg('')` lets an empty identifier silently reach collection endpoints, not the 404 the comment promises
samples.evidence: `seg('')` now returns '' (packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:39-46), so out-of-diff callers build trailing-slash paths. Nest 11 runs Express with `strict routing` disabled, where `/…/documents/` matches the collection route: `packages/backend/src/api/v1/documents.controller.ts:34` (`@Get()` list) is what `HttpClient.getDocument('')` (packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:202) now hits — returning the whole workspace document list where a single-document read was named. Likewise `getCell(doc, tab, '')` (http-client.ts:352-357) resolves to `packages/backend/src/api/v1/cells.controller.ts:45` (`@Get()`), dumping every cell of the tab instead of one ref. Previously both were refused before the request went out. Only the *workspace* segment truly 404s (`/workspaces//…` cannot match `:workspaceId`); identifier segments do not. Fix likely belongs in the new code: keep the empty segment allowed only for `config.workspace` (e.g. a separate `wsSeg()`), and keep refusing it for document/tab/cell/key ids.

samples.summary: New CLI hard-requires an echoed `state`, so it cannot log in against any backend that does not yet echo it (version skew)
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:203-210 rejects any `/callback` whose `state` does not match, and the code is only echoed by the backend change in packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:130-135. `@wafflebase/cli` is a separately published npm binary (packages/cli/package.json:7-9) pointed at arbitrary servers via `--server` / `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER`, and self-hosting is documented (packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:42). Against a backend deployed before this PR the redirect carries no `state`, so the browser shows `State mismatch`, the listener never settles, and `login` fails after the 30s timeout (login.ts:261-269) with a message that names the wrong cause. Nothing pins a minimum server version.

samples.summary: Guard silently drops a `cliState` it does not like, which the new CLI then treats as an injected callback
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:31-34 stores `undefined` when `cliState` is not a string matching `CLI_STATE_PATTERN` — including the ordinary Express case where the param arrives duplicated and `req.query.cliState` is an array (a proxy or a user-copied URL can produce that). The flow then completes but the controller omits `&state=` (auth.controller.ts:130-135), and the CLI listener rejects its own genuine callback (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:203-210), hanging to the 30s timeout. A silently-degraded flow is worse here than a 400 from `/auth/github`.

finding.evidence: `seg('')` now returns '' (packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:39-46), so out-of-diff callers build trailing-slash paths. Nest 11 runs Express with `strict routing` disabled, where `/…/documents/` matches the collection route: `packages/backend/src/api/v1/documents.controller.ts:34` (`@Get()` list) is what `HttpClient.getDocument('')` (packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:202) now hits — returning the whole workspace document list where a single-document read was named. Likewise `getCell(doc, tab, '')` (http-client.ts:352-357) resolves to `packages/backend/src/api/v1/cells.controller.ts:45` (`@Get()`), dumping every cell of the tab instead of one ref. Previously both were refused before the request went out. Only the *workspace* segment truly 404s (`/workspaces//…` cannot match `:workspaceId`); identifier segments do not. verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out. `seg('')` returns '' (url.ts:39-49; DOT_SEGMENT does not match the empty string), and the doc comment at url.ts:31-37 plus test url.test.ts:38-40 assert the empty segment "only produces a path the server 404s on". That promise does not hold for identifier segments: out-of-diff callers http-client.ts:202 and :352-357 build `/documents/` and `.../cells/`, and Nest 11 / Express 5 (backend/package.json:33,36) with default non-strict routing (main.ts never sets 'strict routing') matches a trailing slash — Express 5's router sets `trailing: !opts.strict` (router/lib/layer.js:86-89). `:documentId`/`:sref` cannot match an empty segment, so the request falls to the collection handlers registered earlier: documents.controller.ts:34 (`@Get()` list) and cells.controller.ts:45 (`@Get()` getCells). No guard exists anywhere in between: docs.ts:124-131 and cells.ts:36-40 pass argv values straight through, and http-client.ts has no emptiness check. Result: `docs get ""` returns the whole workspace document list where a single-document read was named. This is in-lane (relaxed validation in an exported symbol with unconsidered out-of-diff consumers) and is not covered by any of the not-my-lane exclusions.

finding.summary: New CLI hard-requires an echoed `state`, so it cannot log in against any backend that does not yet echo it (version skew)
finding.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:203-210 rejects any `/callback` whose `state` does not match, and the code is only echoed by the backend change in packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:130-135. `@wafflebase/cli` is a separately published npm binary (packages/cli/package.json:7-9) pointed at arbitrary servers via `--server` / `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER`, and self-hosting is documented (packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:42). Against a backend deployed before this PR the redirect carries no `state`, so the browser shows `State mismatch`, the listener never settles, and `login` fails after the 30s timeout (login.ts:261-269) with a message that names the wrong cause. Nothing pins a minimum server version.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. The CLI hard-requires an echoed `state`: login.ts:210-214 rejects the callback without settling, and stateMatches (login.ts:168-173) returns false for a null/absent `state`, so a missing parameter is indistinguishable from a wrong one. The only producer of that parameter is the backend change at auth.controller.ts:130-135 (fed by github-auth.guard.ts:31-40); a backend without it redirects to 127.0.0.1/callback with only `code`. The CLI is an independently published binary (packages/cli/package.json:2,7-9) that can be aimed at any server via --server (commands/root.ts:64, login.ts:19) or WAFFLEBASE_SERVER (config/config.ts:92,116,139,156), and self-hosting is a documented deployment (documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:1-24,117-122). Against a pre-PR backend the login hangs and fails at the 30s timeout (login.ts:261-269) with a misleading "Login timed out" message. I found no version negotiation, capability probe, minimum-server pin, or fallback anywhere in packages/cli/src, so no already-guarded ground exists. Only the cited line range was slightly off (210-214 rather than 203-210); the substance is accurate. This is a changed cross-package contract with unupdated consumers, which is in this lens's lane, and major impact is appropriate.

finding.summary: Guard silently drops a `cliState` it does not like, which the new CLI then treats as an injected callback
finding.evidence: packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:31-34 stores `undefined` when `cliState` is not a string matching `CLI_STATE_PATTERN` — including the ordinary Express case where the param arrives duplicated and `req.query.cliState` is an array (a proxy or a user-copied URL can produce that). The flow then completes but the controller omits `&state=` (auth.controller.ts:130-135), and the CLI listener rejects its own genuine callback (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:203-210), hanging to the 30s timeout. A silently-degraded flow is worse here than a 400 from `/auth/github`.

verdict.reason: Verified in the tree. github-auth.guard.ts:31-34 sets `nonce = undefined` for any `cliState` that is not a string matching CLI_STATE_PATTERN (line 15) and still proceeds to createState/`req.__cliStateToken` (35-40) with no rejection. cli-auth.store.ts:38,58 persists and returns the undefined nonce; auth.controller.ts:130-132 then omits `&state=` from the loopback redirect (133-135). The cross-package consumer, packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:210-214, calls stateMatches(expectedState, searchParams.get('state')), which returns false for a null state (login.ts:169) and returns 400 WITHOUT settling the promise, so the genuine callback is discarded and the flow hangs to the 30s timeout at login.ts:261-269. The CLI always mints a conforming nonce (login.ts:40,45-46), so it legitimately assumes the backend echoes it — a violated cross-package invariant, which is in the blast-radius lane and graded major (consumer left broken by the new contract). I found no guard that prevents the failure branch: packages/backend/src/main.ts:65-66 installs only a ValidationPipe (not applied to the raw req.query read in the guard), and there is no `app.set('query parser', ...)` anywhere in packages/backend/src, so a duplicated `cliState` arrives as an array and takes the silent-drop path. No refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: `seg()` rejects the empty string, but `resolveConfig` legitimately yields `workspace: ''` — so every command (and every `--dry-run` preview) now fails with a misleading `Invalid identifier ""` for an unconfigured caller
finding.evidence: `resolveConfig` returns `workspace: ''` on all four resolution paths when no `--workspace`, `WAFFLEBASE_WORKSPACE`, session `activeWorkspace` or profile value exists (packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:100, :125, :147, :163), and `packages/cli/test/config.test.ts:30` asserts exactly that default. `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:106` also persists `activeWorkspace = ''` when the account has zero workspaces, and the comment at config.ts:108 records the empty-workspace state as a known, reachable outcome ("turning every command into a `/workspaces//...` 404"). After this change `apiV1Base()`/`apiKeysUrl()` call `seg(config.workspace)` (packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:50, :62), which throws `Invalid identifier "": a URL path segment cannot be empty, "." or ".."` for that state. Two out-of-diff consequences: (a) every workspace-scoped command for an unconfigured user now reports `{"error":{"code":"ERROR","message":"Invalid identifier \"\"..."}}` instead of the previous auth/404 error, with nothing pointing at the missing workspace config — agents branching on the documented codes in docs/design/cli.md §9 get an undocumented `ERROR`; (b) `--dry-run` previews, which previously succeeded with no config at all (they only formatted a URL), now fail. The fix belongs on the new code: distinguish "workspace not configured" (a clear WORKSPACE_REQUIRED-style error) from "identifier is a dot segment".

verdict.reason: The finding's central premise — that `seg()` rejects the empty string — is not in the code. `packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:13` defines `DOT_SEGMENT = /^(?:\.|%2e){1,2}$/i`, whose `{1,2}` quantifier requires at least one `.`/`%2e`, so `''` does not match and `seg('')` returns `''` (url.ts:39-48, the sole throw is gated on that regex). The error string the finding quotes ("a URL path segment cannot be empty, \".\" or \"..\"") does not exist in the repo — a grep for `cannot be empty` matches only unrelated comment-body validators and vendored node_modules; the real message at url.ts:43-45 says `cannot be "." or ".."`. The empty-segment carve-out is explicit and asserted: url.ts:31-37 documents it, referencing the very `resolveConfig` `workspace: ''` state at issue, and packages/cli/test/url.test.ts:38-40 asserts `seg('') === ''`, with url.test.ts:56-60 and :92-96 asserting `apiV1Base`/`apiKeysUrl` render an unconfigured workspace as `/workspaces/` and `/workspaces//api-keys` rather than throwing. docs/design/cli.md:867-872 records the same decision. The upstream facts are correct (config.ts:100/:126/:147/:164 do yield `workspace: ''`), but neither claimed out-of-diff consequence occurs: workspace-scoped commands still reach the server for the previous auth/404 error, and `--dry-run` previews still format a URL offline. No bypass or broken caller exists.

finding.summary: New empty-segment rejection in `seg()` fires on the *unconfigured workspace* path that `resolveConfig` deliberately produces, breaking every command — including offline `--dry-run` previews
finding.evidence: `resolveConfig` returns `workspace: ''` whenever no `--workspace`, `WAFFLEBASE_WORKSPACE`, session `activeWorkspace` or profile workspace is present — packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:100, :126, :147 and :163 (step 4 is even commented "Nothing available … commands will fail"). Every consumer now routes through `apiV1Base()` → `seg('')`, which throws. Two out-of-diff consequences: (a) the live path that previously produced `/api/v1/workspaces//documents` and a server 404 envelope (documented at packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:108 and packages/cli/test/config.test.ts:102) now dies with `Invalid identifier "": a URL path segment cannot be empty…`, which tells a user nothing about logging in or setting `--workspace`; (b) `printDryRun` (packages/cli/src/client/dry-run.ts:19) also goes through `apiV1Base`, so `wafflebase docs get d1 --dry-run` — a purely offline preview that every skill doc tells agents to run first (packages/cli/skills/docs-manage.md:59) — now throws instead of printing a preview when the user has not logged in yet. No call site supplies a fallback workspace.

verdict.reason: The claimed empty-segment rejection does not exist in `seg()`. The sole guard is `DOT_SEGMENT = /^(?:\.|%2e){1,2}$/i` (packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:13), tested at url.ts:41; the `{1,2}` quantifier requires at least one `.`/`%2e`, so `encodeURIComponent('') === ''` cannot match and `seg('')` returns `''` without throwing. The quoted error text ("a URL path segment cannot be empty") is absent — the actual message (url.ts:43-45) covers only "." and "..", and a grep for empty-checks (`cannot be empty|length === 0|!value`) finds none in src/client/. There is exactly one `seg()` definition repo-wide, so no consumer reaches a stricter variant. The finding's premise about `resolveConfig` returning `workspace: ''` is correct (config.ts:100, :126, :147, :152, :164), but that value passes through `apiV1Base` (url.ts:58) and `printDryRun` (dry-run.ts:18) unchanged, so neither the live `/api/v1/workspaces/` 404 path nor the offline `--dry-run` preview throws. The repo's own tests assert exactly this: `expect(seg('')).toBe('')` (test/url.test.ts:39) and `apiV1Base({...CONFIG, workspace: ''}) === '.../api/v1/workspaces/'` (test/url.test.ts:57-59). Also checked the other builder/consumer sites for a separately-located emptiness precondition that could produce the described symptom: `HttpClient.base` (http-client.ts:86-88) and `apiKeysUrl` (url.ts:68-71) only delegate to `seg()`. No guard exists to bypass or break callers.
